Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the MAP. Quick answers from Acme side:

- Deployment mode: Security prefers a VPC-hosted model for the pilot with customer-managed KMS. We only escalate to on-prem if VPC can't meet our encryption/segmentation requirements.
- Retention: Legal's current preference is 90-day retention for all logs/artifacts from the pilot, with an option to reduce to 30 days conditional on additional DPA clauses.
- PII: Our security team will require that direct identifiers (SSNs, credit card numbers, full passport numbers) are redacted before being sent to the service. Device IDs and hashed user IDs are ok for analytics during evaluation.

Tom (cc) is Acme Security; he'll join the sync to confirm KMS and network constraints. For procurement: we prefer a single PO for the pilot and then conversion to a reserved capacity contract if the pilot meets the SLA/latency targets.

Availability: Thu 5/6 10:00–11:00 PT works for us.

—Sally

Subject: Internal: summary of Acme responses + proposed technical plan

Team — summarizing Acme's answers and my recommendations ahead of the Thu sync: 

Summary from Acme:
- Preference: VPC-hosted with customer-managed KMS
- Retention ask: 90 days (legal), but negotiable to 30 days with DPA addendum
- PII: direct identifiers must be redacted prior to sending

Proposed Redwood approach for pilot:
A) Evaluation environment: provision a VPC-hosted instance in us-west with KMS key material managed by Acme (we support external KMS integration).
B) Data handling: implement a two-layer masking pipeline — client-side redaction for direct identifiers (customer responsibility) + server-side policy that filters token-level retention and strips logs after TTL. Default TTL = 30 days for trial; escalate to 90 days if DPA requires.
C) Metrics: collect latency and token-cost metrics; store only aggregated telemetry tied to hashed ids (no raw PII).

Action items (owner - eta):
- Rishi: draft network requirements doc (v1) and KMS integration checklist (due 5/11)
- Priya: prepare on-prem install checklist as fallback (due 5/14)
- Stephanie: update MAP timeline and add DPA negotiation line (due 5/12)
- Jordan: confirm pilot PO path with procurement at Acme and capture deal conversion conditions (due 5/14)

Target close (decision to run pilot): 5/21/2026 — aligns with Acme procurement windows. If we hit that date we'll schedule a production-readiness review for 6/04/2026.

Notes: If Acme insists on 90-day retention without DPA changes, we need legal to sign off on longer telemetry retention and update pricing for storage.

Rishi
